title: Longest Common Prefix of K Strings After Removal
summary: Given an array of strings and an integer k, for each element in the array, determine the length of the longest common prefix among any k strings from the remaining array after removing the current element.
statement: Given an array of strings and an integer k, for each element in the array, determine the length of the longest common prefix among any k strings from the remaining array after removing the current element. If removing the element results in fewer than k strings, the result for that element is 0. Return an array with these results.
constraints: words is nonempty, k is positive, and lowercase word lengths total at most 100,000.
For each index, remove that word and choose any k remaining words.
Return the maximum common-prefix length attainable by that choice, or zero if fewer than k remain.
hints: Removing one word only invalidates trie nodes on its path whose original count is exactly k.
Count qualifying trie nodes by depth and maintain the greatest nonempty depth in a segment tree.
For each word, decrement depth counts for path nodes with count k, read the maximum active depth, then restore them.
Nodes off the path are unchanged, nodes above k remain qualifying, and every k-word common prefix corresponds to a trie node with count at least k.
editorial: Nodes off the path are unchanged, nodes above k remain qualifying, and every k-word common prefix corresponds to a trie node with count at least k.

tests.explanation: Removing each word produces prefix lengths [3,4,4,3,4].
Removing abd leaves two identical words with prefix length three; removing either abc leaves prefix length two.
